SessionStart._comment: startup and resume ONLY. SessionStart also fires on 'compact', 'clear' and 'fork' — all of which happen mid-conversation on the SAME machine, where there is nothing to restore. Pulling then is at best wasted work and at worst writes over files the running session is using.

SessionEnd._comment: Hooks fire PER CONVERSATION, not per client. 'clear' is excluded: clearing context is not finishing work, and it would push on every /clear. 'resume' IS included, deliberately and after a reversal. It was dropped on 2026-09-07 on the assumption that a resumed conversation always fires a later, non-resume SessionEnd — but Claude Code's docs guarantee no such thing. If a conversation's ONLY SessionEnd ever fires with reason=resume (app force-closed or crashed after a resume), excluding it means that conversation's final state NEVER reaches the remote. That is the one failure this plugin exists to prevent, so the redundant fires are absorbed instead of avoided: a hook-triggered push now RECORDS a request and coalesces onto a single background worker rather than running (or dropping) one per fire — see lib/defer.mjs. The pull/push/pull triplet inside 0.7s that motivated the removal now costs one recorded request, not a lost push. Restored 2026-09-07.
